Senses.Explanation: The Zen lineage as an inherited school and as the field of its recorded matters, questions, and sayings. The term occurs 1,934 times in 285 allowed texts. Yuanwu Keqin gives his own source-and-mind account: 'Buddha's words take mind as the source; when the source is penetrated, speech is also penetrated; therefore it is called the lineage gate' (佛語心為宗。宗通說亦通。既謂之宗門). That explains his use of the first graph; it does not turn every occurrence into a claim about a metaphysical source. Across the corpus, 'within the Zen lineage' occurs 350 times in 108 texts, and 'under the Zen lineage' occurs 175 times in 71 texts. A lecturer whom the Old Recorded Sayings leaves unnamed sets aside the three vehicles and twelve divisions of teaching and asks Muzhou Daoming, 'What is the matter within the Zen lineage?' (三乘十二分教即不問如何是宗門中事). A monk whom the Compendium of the Five Lamps leaves unnamed asks Tianzhu Chonghui to raise and proclaim 'the matter within the Zen lineage' (宗門中事。請師舉唱). Fachang Yiyu draws a line with his staff, sets it aside, and asks Ying Shouzuo how the lineage matter goes (這箇即且止，宗門事作麼生). Wuyi Yuanlai contrasts what he calls the teaching families' utmost reach with 'the strong point within the Zen lineage' (宗門中長處), and elsewhere asks directly what that strong point is. The compound also modifies the title A Collected Anthology of Raising Old Cases in the Zen Lineage (宗門拈古彙集). The title use names a collection belonging to the same lineage; it is not a second referent.
Senses.Note: Definition-formula searches found Yuanwu Keqin's explicit source-and-mind derivation and three occurrences of 'called the lineage gate.' Sixty-three occurrences in 31 texts begin a question with 'what is the Zen lineage' or a longer phrase. The corpus-wide evidence supports one institutional lineage sense across encounter language and collection titles. 'Zen lineage' is preferred because an English reader can identify the referent immediately; 'lineage gate' remains available for passages where the gate image matters.
